# bolero doc should find module documentation

env BOLERO_MODULE=on
env BOLERO_FLAGS=-mod=mod
[short] skip

# Check when module x is inside BOLERO_PATH/src.
bolero doc y
stdout 'Package y is.*alphabet'
stdout 'import "x/y"'
bolero doc x/y
stdout 'Package y is.*alphabet'
! bolero doc quote.Hello
stderr 'doc: symbol quote is not a type' # because quote is not in local cache
bolero list rsc.io/quote # now it is
bolero doc quote.Hello
stdout 'Hello returns a greeting'
bolero doc quote
stdout 'Package quote collects pithy sayings.'

# Double-check when module x is outside BOLERO_PATH/src.
env BOLERO_PATH=$WORK/emptygopath
bolero doc x/y
stdout 'Package y is.*alphabet'
bolero doc y
stdout 'Package y is.*alphabet'

# Triple-check when module x is outside BOLERO_PATH/src,
# but other packages with same import paths are in BOLERO_PATH/src.
# Since bolero doc is running in module mode here, packages in active module
# should be preferred over packages in BOLERO_PATH. See golang.org/issue/28992.
env BOLERO_PATH=$WORK/gopath2
bolero doc x/y
! stdout 'Package y is.*BOLERO_PATH'
stdout 'Package y is.*alphabet'
bolero doc rsc.io/quote
! stdout 'Package quote is located in a BOLERO_PATH workspace.'
stdout 'Package quote collects pithy sayings.'

# Check that a sensible error message is printed when a package is not found.
env BOLERO_PROXY=off
! bolero doc example.com/hello
stderr '^doc: cannot find module providing package example.com/hello: module lookup disabled by BOLERO_PROXY=off$'

# When in a module with a vendor directory, doc should use the vendored copies
# of the packages. 'std' and 'cmd' are convenient examples of such modules.
#
# When in those modules, the "// import" comment should refer to the same import
# path used in source code, not to the absolute path relative to BOLERO_ROOT.

cd $BOLERO_ROOT/src
env BOLERO_FLAGS=
env BOLERO_WORK=off
bolero doc cryptobyte
stdout '// import "golang.org/x/crypto/cryptobyte"'

cd $BOLERO_ROOT/src/cmd/go
bolero doc modfile
stdout '// import "golang.org/x/mod/modfile"'

# When outside of the 'std' module, its vendored packages
# remain accessible using the 'vendor/' prefix, but report
# the correct "// import" comment as used within std.
cd $BOLERO_PATH
bolero doc vendor/golang.org/x/crypto/cryptobyte
stdout '// import "vendor/golang.org/x/crypto/cryptobyte"'

bolero doc cmd/vendor/golang.org/x/mod/modfile
stdout '// import "cmd/vendor/golang.org/x/mod/modfile"'

-- go.mod --
module x
require rsc.io/quote v1.5.2

-- y/y.go --
// Package y is the next to last package of the alphabet.
package y

-- x.go --
package x

-- $WORK/gopath2/src/x/y/y.go --
// Package y is located in a BOLERO_PATH workspace.
package y
-- $WORK/gopath2/src/rsc.io/quote/quote.go --
// Package quote is located in a BOLERO_PATH workspace.
package quote

// Hello is located in a BOLERO_PATH workspace.
func Hello() string { return "" }
